Study objectives: To assess ferritin, Interleukin (IL)-6, and HBD-1 levels during tuberculosis (TB) treatment and evaluate their prognostic value in predicting treatment outcomes

Study objectives: To identify and validate plasma inflammatory markers measured at treatment initiation that predict unfavourable TB treatment outcomes (failure, recurrence, death).
Role of IL-6 in body defense and healing: Higher baseline plasma IL-6 was associated with worse clinical trajectories (treatment failure, recurrence, death). Interpreted as a marker of deleterious/incomplete host inflammatory response that correlates with impaired treatment-related recovery rather than a protective/healing signature.
Study conclusion: Pre-treatment plasma IL-6 is a reproducible biomarker for unfavourable TB outcomes: high baseline IL-6 was linked to increased odds of failure (aOR 2.16), recurrence (aOR 5.36) and death (aOR 4.62) in pooled analysis. Adding baseline IL-6 to a clinical risk model improved discrimination (C-statistic from 0.66 → 0.76).
Future Recommendation: Standardize IL-6 assays across labs, define optimal IL-6 cut-offs for risk stratification, and evaluate point-of-care/clinical use of baseline IL-6 to guide intensified management or targeted host-directed interventions.
